The catalogue

Things that live
beyond the block.

A field guide to the categories of experience that resist being assembled from static content blocks — because they aren't content at all. They're behavior. Each card below has a tiny version running live in its corner.

A / Categories

Eight kinds of more

CAT · 01

Real-time generative visuals

Flow fields, noise, fluid lines — drawn fresh every frame from math, never a saved image. The corner of this card is one such field, looping right now.

In blocks: there is no "render this equation 60×/sec" block.

CAT · 02

Physics & simulation

Gravity, springs, collisions, particle systems. The page maintains a little universe and steps it forward. Objects have momentum and consequences.

In blocks: rectangles don't fall, bounce, or remember velocity.

CAT · 03

Audio synthesis

Oscillators, envelopes, filters — instruments built from the Web Audio graph. No MP3s, just sound generated as you interact.

In blocks: you can embed a player. You can't build the sound.

CAT · 04

Scroll-choreographed story

Pinned scenes, scrubbed animation, progressive reveals tied to scroll progress. The page becomes a timeline you control with the wheel.

In blocks: stacking is vertical order, not a scrubbed timeline.

CAT · 05

Stateful single-page apps

Editors, dashboards, games, tools — anything that holds state, responds to events, and changes without reloading. The page is the application.

In blocks: there's no place to put "the part that remembers."

CAT · 06

Custom interaction & cursors

Magnetic buttons, drag-and-fling, gesture surfaces, bespoke cursors. Interaction designed at the level of the individual frame and pointer event.

In blocks: hover styles, yes. Pointer physics, no.

CAT · 07

Live data & interactive viz

Charts you can brush, attractors you can warp, maps you can drive. Data rendered as something you manipulate, not a flat exported chart image.

In blocks: a static chart embed isn't a data instrument.

CAT · 08

WebGL, 3D & shaders

GPU-driven scenes, raymarched worlds, per-pixel shader effects. Whole rendering pipelines, in the same browser tab, no plugin.

In blocks: there is no fragment-shader content type.

B / Hands-on

Don't take our word for it. Drive it.

Two of the headline exhibits, bigger, with more knobs.

Math · Dataviz live

Interactive data: a Clifford attractor

Thousands of plotted points redrawn every frame, breathing through two animated coefficients. Drag the slider to push the third — the structure reorganizes into something completely new. This is what "interactive visualization" actually means.

Slide to warp the equation in real time

Generative live

One of billions

Seed 0x00000000. Click for the next. A single tiny program, an infinite gallery.

Click the canvas to regenerate

Cursor-reactive live

A field that feels you

Spring-loaded points reacting to the pointer with real vector math. Switch between repel and attract. This is the engine behind every "magnetic" UI moment you've admired.

Move your cursor across the field

Canvas · Physics live

A pocket universe

Drag and fling the balls; momentum is conserved, collisions resolve, walls bounce. A simulation, paused only when off-screen to be kind to your battery.

Drag-and-fling to test the physics

C / Honest scorecard

Right tool, right job

We're not here to dunk. Blocks win plenty of rows — and we say so.

The jobPage-builder / blocksHand-coded web
Ship a marketing page todayBrilliant ✓Overkill ~
Editor-friendly content updatesBrilliant ✓Needs a dev ✗
Consistent design systemGreat ✓Great ✓
Real-time generative graphicsNot a thing ✗Native ✓
Physics / simulationNot a thing ✗Native ✓
Audio synthesisEmbed only ✗Native ✓
Scroll-scrubbed storytellingPlugin-ish ~Native ✓
Stateful app (editor, game, tool)No ✗Native ✓
Custom cursor / magnetic UINo ✗Native ✓
WebGL / 3D / shadersNo ✗Native ✓

The point was never "blocks are bad." It's that more exists, it's open, and it runs in the same browser you're reading this in.
